claude.consequence: Maestro cannot obtain a fresh Claude quota reading on demand
claude.freshness: not controlled by Maestro; the file only advances when some interactive Claude session renders in a directory that has an .orchestrator/
claude.source: .orchestrator/usage.json, written by the operator's Claude Code statusLine command as a side effect of rendering a status line (maestro/backends/claude.py:711 reads only this file)

codex.consequence: Maestro can ask for a reading when it wants one
codex.freshness: controlled by Maestro; the handled form is dated by the rollout, not by the wall clock
codex.source: the run's own rollout file, with app-server as the fallback for when no run is active (maestro/backends/codex.py:1120, :1194)

answer: Not a vendor limitation. Maestro has no pull path for Claude quota at all: it reads a document that an interactive Claude Code statusline render leaves behind as a side effect. Codex, by contrast, is pulled by Maestro on demand.
consequences_for_maestro: QuotaObservation needs an observed_at distinct from written_at, and a staleness bound. A sample older than the bound is censored, not a measurement.
A carried-forward field must be marked as carried forward. An unchanged underlying reading across a pair is 'no new observation', never a zero delta.

Attribution needs an explicit isolation contract before a delta means anything: same unchanged reset epoch across the pair, a non-negative delta, a fresh observation at both ends, and no other session on the pool. The external research also proposed a zero-work control run to measure the probe sequence's own apparent cost; that is worth adopting and is currently in neither the plan nor the review.
Either give Claude a pull path or state in the plan that Claude quota is a push signal Maestro does not control. The current plan implies a symmetry between the backends that does not exist.
findings: The external research was RIGHT that Claude exposes structured five-hour and seven-day percentages with reset timestamps; the sampler reads all four fields. The audit's nulls were a stale/partially-populated document, not an absent vendor surface. The plan's current wording grades the CLI where it should grade Maestro's acquisition path.

The 'post-run sample named Opus 5 rather than the Sonnet review' anomaly is fully explained: the sampler writes the display name of whichever session rendered last. The model field in usage.json is the last renderer's model and must never be used to attribute a reading to an invocation.

The sampler carry-forward merges five_hour/seven_day from the previous file when a render lacks rate limits (a deliberate fix so a parallel session cannot erase a good value). So updated_at is the WRITE time, not the observation time: a percentage can be arbitrarily older than the timestamp beside it.

That makes the proposed before/after delta unsafe in a way that is worse than noise. Two writes can both carry forward the same underlying reading, producing delta = 0 that reads as 'this task consumed nothing' rather than as 'no new observation'.
limits: Source and single-document inspection on this host. No paired experiment was re-run, and the Codex 84 to 89 per cent movement with zero Codex tasks remains explained only as concurrent account use.
Whether the installed claude CLI offers any non-interactive quota surface of its own was not tested; the driver does not use one.
method: Read the acquisition path in source and compared it against the live document. No backend turn.
question: Why did the paired quota sample show Claude with a null reset epoch, a null weekly window and a model name that did not match the run being measured?
